claims.text: The magnitude of local lattice distortions governs the superconducting transition temperature in a single-phase high-entropy alloy.
Local lattice distortions affect Tc by modifying electron–phonon coupling strength.
The proposed starting material is a homogeneous, disordered, single-phase solid solution containing at least five elements at no less than 5 at.% each.
A superconducting Nb–Ti–Zr–Ta–Hf high-entropy alloy is an applicable example of the starting material.
The example starting material may crystallize in a body-centered-cubic lattice.
Annealing or mechanical processing can reduce or enhance local lattice distortions without changing overall composition or causing phase separation.
X-ray diffraction peak broadening can quantify changes in local lattice distortion.
High-resolution TEM or atom-probe tomography can assess local strain fields and short-range ordering.
Atomic-size differences among constituent elements create local strain fields.
Local strain fields alter the phonon spectrum.
Changes in the phonon spectrum alter electron–phonon coupling and the superconducting pairing interaction.
Relevant high-entropy alloys can exhibit conventional isotropic s-wave superconductivity.
Relevant high-entropy alloys can exhibit phonon-mediated superconductivity.
Reducing local lattice distortion by annealing will produce a measurable shift in Tc relative to the as-cast baseline.
If lattice distortions are pair-breaking, reducing them will increase Tc.
Processing that enhances local lattice distortion will cause a Tc trend opposite to that caused by reducing distortion.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to single-phase, disordered, conventional phonon-mediated high-entropy superconductors.
Multiphase or strongly correlated systems may not follow the proposed distortion–Tc trend.
Electron count and disorder may compensate for the influence of lattice distortion on Tc.
A reproducible absence of any Tc shift after a confirmed significant reduction in distortion would falsify the claim that distortion governs Tc under the tested conditions.

contradictions.description: The uncertainty field allows the direction of the Tc change to depend on competing beneficial and pair-breaking effects, but the falsification rule says an opposite trend would falsify the hypothesis. An opposite trend is therefore both allowed by the stated uncertainty and declared falsifying.

The central hypothesis only asserts that distortion magnitude governs Tc through electron–phonon coupling and does not specify a monotonic direction. Consequently, an opposite-direction Tc shift would not by itself falsify the broad governing-mechanism claim.
